templates.text: The $n$th term of a sequence is $[[m]]n - [[c]]$. Work out the 1st, 2nd and 10th terms.

templates.subtopic: Generate a sequence given a simple algebraic rule
templates.source: Y8 Summer B5 Sequences · S2 Generate a sequence given a simple algebraic rule
templates.text: The $n$th term of a sequence is $[[m]]n + [[c]]$. Is [[t]] a term of the sequence? Show how you know.
templates.answer: [[(t - c) % m == 0|if:Yes: n is a whole number/No: n is not a whole number]]: n = ([[t]] − [[c]]) ÷ [[m]] = [[(t - c) / m|dp:2]]

templates.subtopic: nth term of a linear sequence
templates.source: Y8 Summer B5 Sequences · S3 nth term of a linear sequence
templates.text: A sequence has the $n$th term $[[d]]n[[c|signed]]$. Find the 20th term. Then use the $n$th term to say whether [[t]] is in the sequence.
templates.answer: 20th term: [[20 * d + c]]; [[t]] [[(t - c) % d == 0|if:is/is not]] in the sequence

templates.subtopic: Generate a sequence given a complex algebraic rule (E)
templates.source: Y8 Summer B5 Sequences · S4 Generate a sequence given a complex algebraic rule (E)
templates.text: The $n$th term of a sequence is $n^2 + [[c]]$. Which term is equal to [[k * k + c]]?
templates.answer: Term number [[k]] (since [[k * k + c]] − [[c]] = [[k * k]] and $[[k]]^2 = [[k * k]]$)
